extracted.intended_audience: journalists, news producers, reporters, photojournalists, videographers, bloggers, and media seeking NOAA expertise or assets
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how media professionals should request experts, images, statistics, interviews, and topical information from NOAA, and which NOAA office or team to contact for specific subject areas. Includes named contacts, team inboxes, topic scopes, and links to media resources and asset collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use NOAA Communications for media help
rubrics_metrics.description: NOAA Communications is the source for public affairs contacts, NOAA experts, story resources and more; staff work with news producers, digital and print reporters, photojournalists, videographers, bloggers and others on behalf of NOAA's scientific mission areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For requests for experts, images, important statistics, or compelling earth science stories, contact NOAA Communications (e.g., @NOAAComms on X). The office serves as the primary liaison between NOAA science/operations and media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register to receive NOAA news releases and advisories
rubrics_metrics.description: Media should register to receive NOAA news releases and advisories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided registration mechanism on NOAA.gov to obtain news releases and media advisories as they are published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use NOAA Digital Collections for photos and media assets
rubrics_metrics.description: NOAA Digital Collections provides photos and other media assets for stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search NOAA Digital Collections for images and multimedia to support reporting; follow NOAA emblem usage and licensing rules when using assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe NOAA emblem usage and licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: NOAA has rules governing the use of its emblem and licensing of assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before using NOAA logos or materials, review NOAA emblem usage and licensing guidance to ensure compliance with permitted uses and restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact NOAA Headquarters Office of Communications for leadership, policy, budget, legislation
rubrics_metrics.description: NOAA Office of Communications in Washington, D.C. handles interviews with NOAA leadership and information on policy issues, budget, and legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Headquarters contacts for high-level interviews and policy or legislative inquiries rather than technical or operational subject-matter requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: For weather-related questions use National Weather Service press contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Weather-related questions, requests, and media needs should go to the National Weather Service (NWS) contact list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the NWS National Press Office and its listed contacts (e.g., Erica Grow Cei, Marissa Anderson) and team inbox NWS.PA@noaa.gov for operational weather media requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact the National Hurricane Center for tropical storms and hurricanes
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Hurricane Center (NHC) handles media regarding tropical storms and hurricanes in the Atlantic, Caribbean, Gulf of America, and the eastern Pacific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the named NHC media contact (e.g., Maria Torres) and provided phone numbers for interviews and operational briefings on tropical cyclone activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact Storm Prediction Center for severe storms and tornadoes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Storm Prediction Center (Norman, Oklahoma) covers severe storms, tornadoes, and storm chasing topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the SPC media contacts and team inbox (NWS.PA@noaa.gov) for severe-convection related reporting and forecasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact NOAA Satellites (NESDIS) for satellite imagery and environmental data
rubrics_metrics.description: National Environmental Satellite and Information Service (NESDIS) provides satellite images, satellite operations, environmental data, and historical weather and climate data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact NESDIS media (e.g., John Bateman) or nesdis.pa@noaa.gov for queries about satellite-derived products, imagery, and archival datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact NOAA Fisheries (NMFS) for fisheries, protected resources, and marine policy
rubrics_metrics.description: NOAA Fisheries (National Marine Fisheries Service) handles sustainable fisheries (commercial and recreational), protected resources (whales, dolphins, seals and sea turtles), endangered species, habitat, aquaculture, international fishing and marine mammal issues, seafood inspection, Marine Mammal Protection Act, Magnuson–Stevens Act, Endangered Species Act, law enforcement, and ocean fishing regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NMFS media contacts (e.g., Rachel Hager) or NMFS.PA@noaa.gov for stories involving fisheries management, marine species, regulations, and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use regional NOAA Fisheries contacts for localized issues
rubrics_metrics.description: NOAA Fisheries provides regional offices (Alaska, Greater Atlantic, West Coast, Southeast, Pacific Islands) and science centers to handle region-specific marine and fisheries topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the listed regional media leads (e.g., Jennifer Angelo for Alaska, Michael Milstein for West Coast, Allison Garrett/Meaghan Emory for Southeast, Stefanie Gutierrez for Pacific Islands) and regional inboxes (e.g., nmfs.gar.pa@noaa.gov) for area-specific reporting and interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact NOAA Ocean & Coasts (National Ocean Service) for coastal and ocean issues
rubrics_metrics.description: National Ocean Service covers coral reefs, coastal resource management, estuarine research reserves, harmful algal blooms, hazardous spill response and restoration, marine protected areas, marine sanctuaries, nautical charts, ocean observing systems, and tides and water levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reach out to NOAA Ocean & Coasts media (e.g., Alison Gillespie) or oceanservicepress@noaa.gov for coastal resource stories, HABs, charts, tides, and related topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact NOAA Research (OAR) for research topics across climate, weather, ocean, polar, tsunamis
rubrics_metrics.description: Office of Oceanic and Atmospheric Research (OAR) handles NOAA's research activities related to climate, weather, polar, ocean, and coastal research, tsunamis, ocean acidification, global monitoring and observation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use OAR media contacts (e.g., Monica Allen) or oar.pa@noaa.gov for scientific research inquiries, data interpretation, and expert interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact NOAA Ocean Exploration for ocean exploration stories
rubrics_metrics.description: NOAA Ocean Exploration is NOAA's center for activities to explore and better understand the oceans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact Ocean Exploration media leads (e.g., Monica Allen, Emily Crum) for reporting on expeditions, discoveries, and exploration programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact Earth System Research Laboratories for atmospheric science and air quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Earth System Research Laboratories (ESRL) covers atmospheric science, climate change, ozone depletion, weather, and air quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ESRL media contact (e.g., Theo Stein) for specialized atmospheric science and air quality reporting; note location (Boulder, Colorado).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact National Severe Storms Laboratory for radar and severe-weather science
rubrics_metrics.description: National Severe Storms Laboratory handles weather radar, tornadoes, flash floods, lightning, damaging winds, hail and winter weather research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact NSSL media (Norman, Oklahoma) for technical explanations of severe-weather research and technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact Office of Marine and Aviation Operations for ship and aircraft operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Office of Marine and Aviation Operations manages NOAA ship and aircraft operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact OMAO media (e.g., Keeley Belva) or omao.publicaffairs@noaa.gov for stories involving NOAA vessels, aircraft, and operational missions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use team inboxes and listed phone contacts for media requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Many NOAA offices provide team inboxes and phone numbers for media contact and coordination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer team inboxes (e.g., NWS.PA@noaa.gov, nesdis.pa@noaa.gov, NMFS.PA@noaa.gov, oceanservicepress@noaa.gov, oar.pa@noaa.gov, omao.publicaffairs@noaa.gov) for faster routing; phone numbers are provided for urgent operational needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult NOAA topic-specific media resource guides
rubrics_metrics.description: NOAA publishes media resource guides on topical areas (e.g., AI in Hurricane Forecasting; Climate; Deep seabed mineral development; Drought; Extreme heat; Hurricane season; Marine heat waves; Offshore wind energy; Weather modification; Wildfire season and fire weather; NOAA and Wildfire Hub).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these guides for background, expert lists, suggested storylines, and facts/stats when preparing coverage; the guides are linked from the NOAA Communications page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with NOAA via main social media channels
rubrics_metrics.description: NOAA engages with the public and media through its main social media channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NOAA and NOAA Communications on platforms like X and Bluesky for updates, and consider social channels for rapid information or outreach, noting that official briefings and technical data should be coordinated through listed media contacts.
